evaluations.label: A
errors: Names the project 'IS1001c remote control', which never appears in the transcript
States the remote 'will include backlit buttons that activate upon movement'; motion activation was debated and questioned as too costly, not decided
'arched internal structure for component mounting' is invented; the PM said 'odd shaped, with a spongy cover'
'Action Items (none)' contradicts the PM assigning the industrial designer and UI designer to work together on the prototype and the follow-up tasks
Refers to the UI designer as 'UIZ', a label not used in the meeting
strengths: Captures key numbers: wheel sensor about 50x a push button, 12 euro budget
Includes the voice recognition chip email and lists sensible open questions
Outline covers the meeting flow from recap through final concept
weaknesses: Uses 'Speaker 1/2/3/4' in the outline, so readers cannot tell who said what
Empty action items section despite clear next steps
Presents a debated lighting behavior as a specification

evaluations.label: B
errors: Recap lists a 'preview button'; the transcript says 'previous channel button'
Says the group kept the wheel at [11:04]; at that point the PM only said 'maybe', and the decision to keep it came later (around 15:54)
Timestamp [21:24] for asking the designers to work together; that assignment was at about 22:50
'The group did not document a detailed resolution' on left/right handedness understates the PM's conclusion that it works for both hands
strengths: Clear summary with the main decision (yellow banana, wheel on top, buttons on the side) and why
Covers cost figures, the lighting debate, battery concern, plastic cover concern, and the voice chip with 'no decision'
Timestamps and role-based attribution make it easy to check
weaknesses: Action items heading left empty; the assignment appears only in the body
Does not say whether the plastic cover idea was dropped or kept

evaluations.label: C
errors: 'Heart-shaped core with spongy cover suggested'; the PM said 'odd shaped, with a spongy cover'
Gives the UI designer's name as 'UL Hazred'; he said 'Abdul al-Hasred'
'Banana shape proposed' understates that the banana was chosen

Invented action items not assigned in the meeting: 'Facilitate discussion on wheel sensor necessity', 'Assess cost implications of wheel sensor', 'Develop banana-shaped spongy case design' as a separate task
'Simple remote interface confirmed (00:30)' presents the recap of the previous meeting as a new decision
'Provide meeting notes in shared folder (00:00)'; the PM said notes would be in his folder, and the shared folder was where the UI designer's slides were
strengths: Includes the 50x cost ratio and 12 euro budget
Notes the left/right hand discussion and lighted buttons to identify the side
Lists per-role tasks, including the designers' joint prototype work
weaknesses: Leaves out the voice recognition chip email entirely
Does not clearly state final decisions (wheel kept, banana chosen, spongy cover)
Action list padded with inferred tasks, and some timestamps are wrong

evaluations.label: D
errors: 'hard internal structure with spongy outer cover'; 'hard' is not stated, the PM said 'odd shaped, with a spongy cover'
'recess or offset channel buttons slightly'; the UI designer said to put them 'a bit out of the way', and recessing them was not mentioned
Splits the joint assignment into separate tasks for the industrial designer (final banana design) and the UI designer (layout), which is inferred, not stated
strengths: Complete recap of the previous meeting's decisions
Clear component decisions: standard battery, chip, wheel kept despite 50x cost, 12 euro limit
Correctly marks open items: plastic cover reconsidered, light trigger debated, voice chip deferred
Banana decision with its reasons, construction, and left/right handedness outcome; well-organized next steps
weaknesses: Leaves out the wheel push-down idea
Says 'Backlit buttons confirmed' a little too firmly given the open trigger debate

rationale: D is the most complete and best organized. It shows what was decided and what stayed open, and it has only small embellishments. B is accurate and well grounded with timestamps, but it has a 'preview button' slip, an early-timed wheel decision and an empty action items heading. A covers the substance but invents a project code and an internal structure, presents motion-activated lighting as decided, uses anonymous speaker labels and lists no action items. C misquotes 'heart-shaped', garbles the name, leaves out the voice chip, does not state the final decisions firmly and pads its action items with invented tasks.
